small_guidance:
- The current gather has a hot inner loop where each (kd,kh,kw) re-checks stride divisibility. Since STRIDE=2 and PAD=1 are constexpr, split the program grid by output-spatial parity: precompute that for any fixed (od,oh,ow) only kd≡(od+PAD)%STRIDE etc. contribute, so collapse the 3×3×3=27 inner taps to the ~8 that actually fire. This roughly 3× reduces tl.dot calls.
- Add autotune configs with BLOCK_SP=32 / BLOCK_OC=128 and BLOCK_SP=64 / BLOCK_OC=128 (num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4). With OC=64 the OC tile can cover OC fully in one program — drop the OC grid dim and let BLOCK_OC=64 statically, freeing more occupancy for the SP axis.
- Hoist `in_spatial_off` and `spatial_valid` per (kd,kh,kw) outside any branch and use `tl.multiple_of`/`tl.max_contiguous` hints on `sp_offs` so the per-tap input gather can coalesce on the W axis.
large_guidance:
- Switch from gather-style "for each output, find contributing inputs" to scatter-style "for each input voxel, scatter-add input × weight outer product into KD·KH·KW output locations." Input volume is 8× smaller than output (stride=2), so the K-loop is 8× shorter and the divisibility masking disappears entirely. Use atomic adds into a zero-initialized accumulator, then a second small kernel applies bias + add_input + hardswish epilogue. On Ada/Ampere fp32 atomics into global are fast enough given the sparse write pattern (each input contributes to disjoint output cells when stride==kernel_size-1 case, but still only 27 writes per input).
- Alternative without atomics: reformulate as an im2col-style GEMM where the K dimension is (IC × valid_taps_per_output). Since stride=2 and kernel=3, every output position has a fixed set of (at most 8) valid (kd,kh,kw) triples determined purely by (od%2, oh%2, ow%2). Launch 8 specialized kernels (one per parity class) each doing a dense GEMM of shape [DHW_out/8, OC] × [OC, IC·num_taps]; no masking, no wasted FMAs.
- Use channels-last (NDHWC) layout for both input and output so the GEMM-K (IC) axis is contiguous in memory — the current NCDHW layout forces strided loads of stride DHW_in across the IC dim, which is the main bandwidth bottleneck. Pre-permute weight to [KD,KH,KW,IC,OC] once in __init__.
